findings.message: Scope in and the third criterion require integrate to get `reviewed_sha` through `Merge._approval`'s validation path. That path demands `verdict == approve` and `pinned == head`. Integrate runs after `MergeQueue` has rebased the candidate worktree, which moves `refs/heads/<stem>` and the worktree `HEAD` off the reviewed sha. `Candidate` carries only stem, branch, worktree and run_seq, not the pre-rebase head, and `squatch/mergequeue.py` is out of the fence. So a correctly approved candidate is always refused as stale. The criteria (approval path equivalence, correct integration, stale/missing refusal) cannot all be met as specified.
findings.paved_road: Name the head the approval is pinned against without editing mergequeue.py. For example, have integrate resolve the pre-rebase head through existing `Git.rev_parse` (such as the worktree's `ORIG_HEAD` left by the rebase), or have the regate adapter record it, then call `Merge._approval(stem, pre_rebase_head)`. Add a criterion proving that a fresh approve pinned to the pre-rebase head integrates and that a stale pin is refused.

findings.message: Scope in says integrate uses 'the same journal approval lookup ... as `Merge._approval`'. `Merge._approval` does not read the journal. It parses the on-disk ticket-plane record `tickets/<stem>/review.md` with `load_review`. An implementer following the scope text would build a journal lookup, a second approval path that the Definition of rejected forbids.
findings.paved_road: Change the wording to 'the same on-disk `tickets/<stem>/review.md` approval check (`Merge._approval`)' so scope in matches merged behavior.
